negative_findings.description: Neither Semos (semos.com.mk) nor Duna (duna.mk) nor Edusoft (edusoft.com.mk) exposes a discoverable banking-specific 'references' or 'clients' page in search results. Semos surfaced mainly through careers pages and its Semos Education arm; Duna through retail/fiscal and public-sector projects; Edusoft through vertical marketing pages that claim finance/insurance expertise without naming customers.
negative_findings.result_summary: mk-language queries combining each company name with банкарски софтвер / референци / банка returned company profiles, job ads and directory entries — no named bank end-customers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For these three seed actors the indirect route (bank-side press, app metadata, tender awards, LinkedIn project mentions) will have to substitute for vendor reference lists; do not conclude they have no bank business.

negative_findings.description: The Netcetera global references index page lists ~9 visible case studies (Atruvia, Finnova, Stet, Valiant, Klar, Zak/Bank Cler, SIX, Viseca, PostFinance) and claims 2190 client projects, but shows no Southeast Europe / North Macedonia entries on the index itself.
negative_findings.result_summary: The MK-relevant Halkbank reference exists at a deep URL (/references/Halkbank.html) reachable only via search, not via the index page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deep-linked reference pages are invisible to index-only crawling; collection must enumerate the /references/ slug space or rely on search, or MK evidence will be systematically missed.

negative_findings.description: A Macedonian-language search for ATM/POS hardware distributors and service partners in MK (NCR, Diebold Nixdorf and similar) returned only bank ATM-locator pages and generic ATM maps, no named local distributor or maintenance partner.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries on банкомати / дистрибутер / сервис / партнер produced zero channel-company results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The self-service hardware channel is a core Printec-adjacent segment and is currently an evidence hole for MK; it needs a different attack (public procurement notices, bank tender awards, hardware-vendor partner locators, service-company registry codes).

negative_findings.description: Sorsix, IT Labs and Interworks — frequently cited MK software houses — could not be tied to banking or payments clients in this pass; searches returned generic company profiles, Glassdoor/SourceSeek entries and unrelated bank Wikipedia pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: No finance-vertical evidence found for these three actors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: They should stay on the long-list as unconfirmed rather than be either promoted or discarded; a targeted mk-language pass per company is needed.

negative_findings.description: The current corporate domain for ASEE North Macedonia (post-rebrand from ASSECO SEE) was not confirmed; searches routed to directory entries (zk.mk), a news item about the rebrand, and DevelopmentAid rather than the company's own MK site. Same for Ultra's corporate domain.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two significant local channel actors are documented only through third-party profiles.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ASEE is likely the single largest banking-software supplier in the MK channel; leaving its primary site unresolved would leave the biggest competitor node uncovered.

negative_findings.description: https://www.semos.com.mk/ returned a 'Parse Error: Invalid header token' and https://masit.org.mk/en/members-en/ returned HTTP 404 (the real path is /en/members-of-masit/ per the site menu).
negative_findings.result_summary: Two fetch failures, both attributable to server header quirks / wrong path guesses rather than dead sites; individual MASIT member slugs under /members-mk/ and /en/members-en/ do resolve in search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These must be recorded as unverified, not dead; a retry with a browser user-agent and the correct listing path is required.

coverage_gaps.description: No evidence found for the ATM / self-service / POS hardware reseller and maintenance channel in North Macedonia — who distributes and services NCR, Diebold Nixdorf, Wincor, and cash-handling equipment for MK banks.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Attack via (a) e-nabavki.gov.mk public procurement for the state-owned/development bank and public institutions, (b) hardware vendors' own partner locators filtered to MK, (c) MK company registry activity codes for computer-equipment servicing, (d) bank annual-report supplier notes.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one vendor partner directory (Thales CPL) was actually reached. Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, Cisco, Entrust, Temenos, Salesforce, UiPath and Diebold partner locators were not queried for North Macedonia, yet these are the definitive source of partner STATUS and tier for local integrators.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a systematic country=North Macedonia sweep of the top 15 vendor partner finders and record firm, tier, competencies and effective dates; this is a repeatable deterministic collection job.

coverage_gaps.description: Macedonian search worked well for actor discovery (банкарски софтвер, електронско банкарство, референци) but produced almost nothing for partner-status vocabulary — овластен партнер, сертифициран партнер, златен партнер, дистрибутер, имплементациски партнер were not systematically exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated mk query wave on partner/tier vocabulary plus Albanian-language variants (partner i autorizuar, zgjidhje bankare) — Albanian is a second official language and was not used at all in this pass.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell approached the vendor→bank link only from the integrator side. Bank-side artefacts that name suppliers — annual reports, e-banking terms & conditions, mobile app privacy policies, TLS certificate and DNS records of banking portals — were not examined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a bank-side pass: parse MK bank annual reports and e-banking T&Cs for supplier names, and fingerprint banking portals (HTTP headers, JS bundles, cert issuers) to attribute platforms to vendors.

coverage_gaps.description: Newly discovered or partially discovered actors — Melon Solutions, Ultra, Ентаер лоџик ДИТ, БЦС, Accent, SoftNET, Aitroniks, Sorsix, IT Labs, Interworks, Akton, Login Systems, Revoit — have no confirmed finance references yet.

coverage_gaps.description: Several of the strongest artefacts found are point-in-time (a 2020 INREKOM e-banking study, individual news items). No continuous feed was established for vendor–bank announcements.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up recurring keyword monitors on bankarstvo.mk, it.mk and smartportal.mk using mk trigger terms (имплементира, лансираше, партнерство, нова платформа, решение) with entity extraction into a vendor–bank pairing table.

brief: The MK local-integrator channel is documented far better in Macedonian trade media and business directories than on the integrators' own websites: zk.mk's 'Електронско банкарство' category and MASIT's member registry are the two best pointer sources, while bankarstvo.mk, it.mk and smartportal.mk regularly name the vendor behind a bank's launch (e.g. Komercijalna Banka's new e-banking portal attributed to Nextsense). Only three local actors publish genuine reference material of their own — Nextsense (news items naming Komercijalna Banka and ProCredit), Aspekt (a full customers page of core-banking and microfinance case studies) and Netcetera (a deep-linked Halkbank North Macedonia wallet reference) — whereas the named seed actors Semos, Duna and Edusoft expose no bank references at all and must be tracked indirectly. The highest-yield untapped techniques are vendor partner directories filtered to North Macedonia (Thales already lists Nextsense) and app-store publisher metadata, which attributes MK bank apps to their real supplier (NLB mKlik ships under an Asseco package namespace). The two serious holes are the ATM/POS hardware reseller-and-service channel, for which mk-language search returned nothing at all, and the unresolved corporate domain of ASEE North Macedonia, probably the largest banking-software supplier in the local channel.
